$comment: THE PROVIDER POOL. The only place in this platform where a model provider is named.
Provider routing is mandated at the AI Gateway (specification 13.5), which is why a
provider-neutral model port exists before a second provider does: a second provider is
architecturally assumed, and this file is where it will be added.
WHAT ADDING A PROVIDER COSTS. An entry below, a role assignment for the gateway's identity on
the new resource, and nothing else. No agent, governance, retrieval or execution code names a
provider, so none of it changes (FR-OPS-009). If adding one ever requires touching RagCore,
the boundary has been drawn wrong and the fix belongs here rather than there.
NO CREDENTIAL APPEARS IN THIS FILE AND NONE CAN. Every backend authenticates by the gateway's
managed identity; build/policy/azure-identity.json names AzureKeyCredential, api_key and
OPENAI_API_KEY as forbidden configuration for the `foundry` resource, and
ragcore/tests/security/test_azure_identity.py scans committed build/**/*.json for exactly the
shapes a credential takes.

egressRule.statement: RagCore -> AI Gateway -> model provider. No component reaches a model provider directly (FR-OPS-007, constitution §Model access).
enforcedBy: ragcore/src/ragcore/model/egress.py — ModelEgressPort is the only shape a call takes
ragcore/tests/architecture/test_no_direct_model_call.py — no provider SDK or endpoint outside model/
ragcore/src/ragcore/config/settings.py — ModelGatewaySettings has no provider, key or model-endpoint field

$comment: The pool the policy routes to. One member today; the pool exists rather than a single
backend because a pool with one member and a pool with three are the same policy line,
and a single backend promoted to a pool later is a policy change under time pressure.

credentials.$comment: The gateway's own identity, onward to Foundry. Not a key, and not the caller's identity — the gateway is a policy function, not an identity boundary (plan §Trust boundaries).

circuitBreaker.$comment: A provider having a bad minute becomes a fast refusal rather than a queue of calls each holding part of a fifteen-minute execution window.

$comment: Used by llm-semantic-cache-lookup to embed the incoming prompt, and by the platform's own
embedding calls. It is a SEPARATE backend rather than the completion pool because the
cache must keep working while the completion pool's circuit breaker is open — otherwise
one provider outage disables the cache that would have absorbed part of it.

backends.$comment: Azure AI Content Safety, reached by the gateway's managed identity with the Cognitive Services User role. Required by llm-content-safety in both directions.

$comment: APIM named values, resolved at deployment. Those marked keyVault are read by APIM's own
managed identity (id-synthia-apim). NONE of them is a model provider credential.
The three numeric ones are the per-organisation budget. They are deliberately deployment
configuration rather than application settings: a budget an application could read is a
budget an application could be asked to work around.

ai-gateway-audience.why: The audience RagCore's token must carry.

ragcore-identity-object-id.why: The one caller permitted. Object id of id-synthia-ragcore.

semantic-cache-seconds.why: Cache entry lifetime. Redis is transient only; every entry expires.

$comment: REDIS IS TRANSIENT ONLY (constitution Principle IV, plan §Platform environment). It is the
semantic cache's store and is never an authority and never a durable record.
Two consequences, both deliberate: every entry carries a TTL, and no sample flow reads the
cache. A lost cache costs model calls and nothing else — which is the test of whether a
store is really transient, and this one passes it.
The cache is partitioned by organisation through the policy's vary-by. Without that, a
completion produced for one organisation could be served to another: a cross-tenant leak
through a cache, which no database-level isolation would catch.
